newsitem.title: MEXICO: U.S. embassy identifies four dead in Mexico crash.
newsitem.headline: U.S. embassy identifies four dead in Mexico crash.

text.p: Three U.S. citizens and a Briton died when a small private plane crashed in the central Mexican state of Zacatecas, U.S. embassy officials said on Thursday.

The plane slammed into a mountain in stormy weather on Tuesday night after leaving El Paso, Texas en route for the central Mexican city of Toluca, Monterrey U.S. consulate officer Steve Holgate told Reuters.
Holgate said the deceased were the pilot and officials from Virotest PLC, a biotechnical company incorporated in the Britain and the United States, on a business trip to Mexico.
Company chief executive officer Corey Graber and his assistant Gretchen Lyons were on the plane, both from Carmel, California, he said.
Company officer Vernon Spencer from London and pilot Mike Kirkpatrick from Oklahoma were also on board, Holgate said.
The cause of the crash had not been determined, embassy officials said. Mexico's Communications and Transport Ministry said the plane was a Aerocommander 1121 B.
